trends.name: Iran-Hormuz Strait Escalation Risk
trends.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister explicitly rejected Trump's ceasefire demands regarding Strait of Hormuz control, with Iranian Revolutionary Guards attacking oil tanker in Qatari waters. This escalates geopolitical risk for oil markets and shipping, with Iran signaling it will decide Hormuz's future alongside Oman only. Critical for energy prices and global supply chains.

trends.name: Oil Market Volatility & Energy Security
trends.summary: Global oil prices holding above $100 amid Iran tensions despite de-escalation rhetoric, with Hormuz closure risk threatening supply. Energy stocks like Murphy USA benefiting from war premium. Fuel surcharges hitting consumer behavior and cruise line pricing, signaling inflationary pressures.

trends.name: SpaceX IPO & Mega IPO Wave
trends.summary: SpaceX confidentially filed for IPO, potentially setting stage for record offering and sparking broader wave of jumbo IPOs in 2026. This signals strong capital markets appetite and could reshape aerospace/defense sector valuations and investor positioning.

trends.name: Nike Demand Collapse & Guidance Cut
trends.summary: Nike shares tumbled on soft guidance with analyst commentary noting 'disappointing China sales' and conditions 'getting worse before better.' Signals potential consumer weakness in premium athletic wear and China demand deterioration impacting multinational retailers.

trends.name: Tech Cyber Attacks & Iran Threats
trends.summary: Iran threatened Nvidia, Apple, and other tech giants with attacks; reports of Iranian strikes on Amazon Web Services servers in Bahrain. Creates systemic risk for cloud infrastructure, semiconductor supply chain, and enterprise IT continuity planning.

trends.name: AI/Crypto Investment Boom Continues
trends.summary: Ark Invest leading OpenAI's latest funding round with Cathie Wood backing AI infrastructure; Franklin Templeton expanding crypto offerings via CoinFund spinoff acquisition. Institutional capital flowing aggressively into AI and cryptocurrency despite volatility, signaling confidence in secular tech trends.

trends.name: Intel Recovery & Semiconductor Strength
trends.summary: Intel shares jumped 10% after buying back its Ireland chip fab, signaling renewed manufacturing confidence and U.S. reindustrialization momentum. Shows chipmakers gaining leverage amid geopolitical supply chain concerns and AI infrastructure demand.

trends.name: GLP-1 Pill Market Expansion
trends.summary: FDA approved Eli Lilly's GLP-1 oral medication, opening next phase of weight-loss drug market beyond injectables. Expands addressable market significantly and could shift competitive dynamics from Ozempic/Wegovy dominance to broader pharmaceutical access.

trends.name: Manufacturing Momentum & Economic Resilience
trends.summary: U.S. manufacturing sees best month in 2.5 years with S&P Global PMI at 52.3; private sector hiring beat at 62,000 in March. Signals economic resilience, though Iran war threatens to derail progress. Critical for Fed policy signaling and growth vs. inflation debate.

trends.name: Activist Investing & Strategic Pivots
trends.summary: Snap shares surged on activist letter signaling turnaround catalyst; Quanta Services upgraded for U.S. reindustrialization leadership. Activist investors targeting value opportunities amid market dislocations, creating M&A and restructuring catalysts.

trends.name: Dollar Weakness & Currency Volatility
trends.summary: U.S. Dollar index experiencing worst 2-day slide since January, impacting intermarket dynamics heading into Q2. Weakens dollar-denominated assets but benefits exporters and emerging markets, signaling potential shift in carry trade positioning.

trends.name: Birthright Citizenship & Political Risk
trends.summary: Supreme Court hears Trump's birthright citizenship challenge with Trump present; separate effort launched to remove Trump's name from federal property. Creates legal uncertainty for immigration policy and potential market impacts on labor supply, demographics, and policy regime shifts.
